verdict.label: STEP ASIDE (IMPROVING) — SPX Clears 7,480 Trigger; Semis +12%/AMD +8%; Upgrade Clock Day 1 of 2; GOOGL/TSLA Binary Wednesday AH
verdict.headline: Semiconductor stocks surge to records while Iran tanker attack keeps oil elevated
verdict.rationale_short: The S&P 500 closed at 7,509, the first close above the 7,480 formal upgrade trigger — starting the two-session confirmation clock. The session was semiconductor-led: Micron surged 12.2% on Morgan Stanley's 25% DRAM-price forecast, SanDisk rose 7.6%, and AMD extended its Microsoft Helios gains a second day, closing +7.9% to $543 at 52-week highs. VIX settled at 17.05, marginally above the 17 formal threshold. WTI settled near $83.90 — elevated but off intraday highs — as Iran attacked a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz and Houthis declared a maritime embargo against Saudi Arabia. 10Y Treasury yield reached 4.63%, highest since mid-May, as oil-driven inflation fears resurfaced. September hike probability remained at 48.7% (below the 60% formal trigger). GOOGL and TSLA report Wednesday AH; the outcome resolves the most important binary of Q2 earnings season and determines whether the 7,480 SPX break was structural.

bear_case: Counter-thesis: The July 21 rally was memory-led short-covering, not broad AI infrastructure confirmation. Micron's 12% surge responded to a Morgan Stanley price FORECAST, not actual HBM or DRAM pricing data — the market has priced in 25% DRAM gains before a single invoice confirms them. AMD's +11.7% two-day surge on the Microsoft Helios contract is one deployment agreement for H2 2026; it does not quantify or refute Kimi K3 AI-demand-disruption at scale. AMD AI Day Day 1 (July 22) is the setup day; if Lisa Su's keynote on July 23 fails to deliver additional hyperscaler wins or competitive MI450 pricing vs H100/B200, a two-day +12% run could unwind rapidly. WTI settling near $83.90 — even with Iran tanker attack and Houthi maritime embargo active — means any diplomatic breakdown that spikes Brent to $90+ (as occurred on July 20 post-close) can re-engage the BEARISH oil trigger within hours. The 10Y yield rising to 4.63% (highest since mid-May) on the same day equities rallied is a warning signal: risk-on and inflation-risk premia are expanding simultaneously, which is unsustainable. A GOOGL Cloud miss on July 22 AMC would immediately test whether the 7,480 SPX break was structural or a one-session short-squeeze overshoot, resetting the upgrade clock and potentially extending the STEP ASIDE regime. Invalidation: GOOGL Cloud revenue growth exceeds 22% YoY AND TSLA gross margin exceeds 15% on Wednesday confirms the July 21 SPX break was structural, not a squeeze.
